answer: A trellis of escalating bonds stops cheap identities: each new account must lock a deposit that grows steeply with every sibling identity sharing its hardware fingerprint, and the deposit only unlocks after a probation window of verified useful work. A raven audit, a random unannounced spot check by an independent verifier, can slash the whole ladder if any rung faked its work. An attacker standing on the ledge of one real machine therefore pays a rising, forfeitable price per fake, while an honest newcomer pays one small bond once.
